findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the ordering and state-lock/quiescence contract between this apply, the 'rubied' MCP-PAT apply, and the historical-version scrub, so no apply writes a new tfstate version during (or after) the scrub of the shared object.
evidence: 'Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the state scrub covers those params too'
'Permanently delete the affected object versions ... s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate (bucket versioning, ~149 versions)'
Two applies against one shared tfstate object plus a destructive version-delete is a check-then-act TOCTOU unless ordering + state-lock quiescence is defined.
findings.finding: The plan coordinates with a SEPARATE 'rubied' terraform apply seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params, and both applies mutate the SAME remote tfstate object (s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate), plus the historical-version scrub deletes object versions of that same state file — but the plan never states the concurrency/ordering contract (terraform state lock acquisition, which apply runs first, and whether the version-scrub is quiesced against in-flight writes) so the two operations do not race or scrub a version another apply is mid-write on.
findings.location: Coordination section / Step 4 (SCRUB the historical cleartext)
scenarios: 'rubied' apply writes a new tfstate version while this ticket's scrub is enumerating/deleting versions, leaving a fresh cleartext version un-scrubbed or corrupting the state lock.
Both applies contend for the terraform state lock and one fails mid-apply, leaving prod partially migrated.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence explicitly: (a) both applies complete and acquire/release the terraform state lock in a defined order, (b) confirm no in-flight writers, (c) THEN enumerate+delete historical versions as the final step, and re-verify version count post-scrub.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound and sequence the reset->reseed gap explicitly (e.g. maintenance-window freeze on instance launches/consumer restarts until all slots re-seeded) and require every consumer to re-materialize (fetch-secrets.sh) and restart so the rotation is actually in effect before close.

The plan handles boot-time consumers via the user_data.sh fail-fast but does not address ALREADY-RUNNING consumers still holding the old value in their on-box 0600 .env, nor bound the reset->reseed gap — this is the dual-write/cutover window in T11(d).
